text.p: Portuguese cash bonds firmed and futures rose after a series of statements from European government officials who denied knowledge of any plan to delay entry of the so-called "Club Med" countries to the first stage of Economic and Monetary Union.

Dealers said the market remained nervous about EMU entry for Italy, Spain and Portugal but the official denials from Germany, France, Italy and Spain had lent support. They said spreads with 10-year Spanish Bonos would remain flat.
The escudo recovered after the comments too, rising to 100.36/39 per mark from an opening 100.67/70.
